subject: MSA brand & confidentiality: redlines and sign-off plan
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@inkline.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Bates <oliver.bates@inkline.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA review: brand & confidentiality items

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for sending the latest MSA. Our legal and marketing teams ran a quick pass and surfaced three items that need alignment before procurement can issue the PO:

1) Logo / co-branding usage: request for a limited crediting window (90 days) for customer case studies and a mandatory review step for any joint press release.
2) Confidentiality carveouts: marketing wants a narrow reference exception for publicly available performance metrics; legal asks that this be explicitly scoped to prevent competitive disclosure.
3) Public announcement embargo: request a 14-day embargo from contract effective date to allow coordinating internal comms.

I've attached InkLine's redline summary and a SOC2 snapshot they asked to see. Can we set a 30-minute sync next week to go through the tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Connors
Head of Partnerships, InkLine Inc.
attachments: InkLine_redline_summary.docx (docx), SOC2_snapshot_Q2_2028.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: MSA review: brand & confidentiality items

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the detailed pass and the SOC2 snapshot — helpful. I've looped Marissa from Legal Ops to get us a proposed approach for each point. Quick notes before the sync:

- Logo / co-branding: Redwood is comfortable with a 90-day promotional credit period for case studies, but we need the right to extend in writing for joint campaigns. We'll propose language that preserves that flexibility.
- Confidentiality exception: we can agree to a tightly scoped exception for "publicly available metrics" but would need an explicit definition and a carveout for any metric derived from shared tokenized data.
- Embargo: 14 days is reasonable; we may request an earlier release if both parties mutually sign off.

Can you do Tue 24 Jul, 10:00am PT? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a one-page checklist we can walk through.

Best,
Chloe

Team — forwarding InkLine's summary ahead of Tue's sync. I drafted proposed redline snippets and an internal checklist (attached) to guide the call. High-level position: we can meet InkLine on the publicity window and embargo with the following guardrails.

Proposed redline bullets (high priority for legal review):
- Limited publicity credit: change "indefinite" to "90 days from effective date, with written extension subject to mutual agreement".
- Case study approval: add a "reasonable review" clause with a 5-business-day review SLA for accuracy/branding; no unreasonably withheld approvals.
- Confidential metrics carveout: define "publicly available metrics" as items published on public web pages or in investor filings; exclude any metric computed from data shared under the agreement.
- Embargo exceptions: allow earlier release by mutual written consent; include contact points for PR approvals.

Attachments: MSA_brand_confidentiality_checklist.xlsx; InkLine_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (I incorporated Harvard-style redlines for the above).

Please review before Tue. Karthik, please flag anything product-related (metrics or derived data) we should push back on. Kimberly, can you review the publicity SLA and advise on acceptable risk for marketing?

—Marissa

Thanks for the notes and for sending Marissa's checklist ahead of the call — that made the sync efficient. Per our discussion, attaching our redline to show the places we still want tightened (InkLine_Redlines_Final.docx). Three quick clarifications from our side after the call:

1) We can accept the 90-day promotional window but request that the customer credit includes a single-line attribution in the specific piece of collateral (no logos in perpetuity).
2) For the confidentiality carveout, we need stronger language excluding any metrics that rely on token-level data or non-public customer configurations.
3) Embargo: we can agree to 14 days but will require a 48-hour heads-up prior to publication to allow technical signoff.

I've attached our final redline + the SOC2 snapshot we referenced in the sync. Looking forward to Marissa's final suggested text.

Subject: Re: MSA brand & confidentiality: redlines and sign-off plan

Sarah / Oliver —

Thanks again for the productive call and for turning the redline around. Marissa and Kimberly have approved the language below which we believe addresses both parties' needs:

- Promotional window: 90 days from Effective Date; Redwood may request an extension for joint campaigns with InkLine's written consent.
- Case study approval: 5-business-day review window; approval not to be unreasonably withheld; attribution limited to a one-line credit in specified collateral.
- Confidentiality carveout: "publicly available metrics" limited to those published on public investor or product pages; explicitly excludes metrics derived from shared token-level data or customer-specific configurations.
- Embargo: 14 days standard; 48-hour technical signoff notice required for publication.

Next steps: I will upload the final redline to Drive and send a DocuSign envelope today. Please review the DocuSign preview at the link below and indicate any last-minute edits in the next 24 hours. If there are no edits, procurement can route the PO once the signed MSA is back.
